implementerProof.how: TestAnEventCommittedWhileItsOwnerIsInFlightIsReadWhenThatOwnerIsBack and TestAnOwnerLeftForTheBatchsEndLogsItsFailureOnce pass 20 of 20 at 2678be4b and fail 20 of 20 on 9cabeaf6's code with the head's owner_lane_test.go (owner_lane_test.go:202 'did not carry event 3 within 8s of its commit ... the scan read past its owner and then waited for a back-off'; owner_lane_test.go:285 'logged 2 publish lines for one attempt at event 2, want one'). The tester's TestAHolderThatNeverAnswersDoesNotDelayAnotherIssuesEvents passes 20 of 20. The outbox package passes under CGO_ENABLED=1 -race; outbox, duty, store, bus and multiprocess ok; build, vet, gofmt and infra vets clean; the connection-count test passes.

proof.criterion: An event committed for an owner while that owner is in flight under a silent holder is published once the owner is released, not after its back-off; one log line per failed attempt
proof.surface: real envoy-dispatch built at 2678be4b (and at 9cabeaf6 as the control) on a real nats-server 2.10.29, holders registered through the role and session buckets: RH-1 routed to a live holder that never answers, RH-2 to one that answers
proof.command: inflight.sh: RH-1's route event e1 waits for a back-off of at least 3 s; its attempt_count is raised to 8 there (so its next back-off is 4 min 20 s); 1 s into that retry's receipt wait one PATCH sets RH-1's parent to RH-3, committing RH-1 issue.updated (e2) and RH-3 child.added together, so the batch the commit wakes reads RH-3 and skips RH-1; then the time until e2's issue-topic copy is recorded
proof.observed: Head: e2 reached notifications.dispatch.issue.RH-1.issue.updated 3.917 s after its commit, when e1's batch ended (e1 backed off to 02:56:06, attempt 9). e1 logged 4 ERROR 'dispatch outbox: publish event' lines for its 4 attempts. The control on 9cabeaf6 did not reproduce the old defect live in 4 variants (3.885 s with the two-issue write, 3.490 s with 2 s of traffic on four other issues, 4.146 s and 1.701 s without): each time a later batch read nothing and set missed. The defect's narrow interleaving (every batch in the window reads some other owner whose send also fails) is reached by the unit test, which fails 20 of 20 at 9cabeaf6 and passes 20 of 20 here. Live logs on both builds showed one line per attempt; the double line needs the released-or-deadline settle path, which the unit test reaches.
proof.negativeControl: 9cabeaf6's code fails both new tests 20 of 20.
